lawyer:
SMG Amirullah Chowdhury with Abul Hossain Azadi, Advocates -For the Appellants 
Snigdha Huq, Assistant Attorney-General -For the State
parties:
Zahed alias Zahed Ali & ors ------ Appellants
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 9. Mr Chowdhury, first of all, has taken us through the first information report, the depositions of the witnesses, the charge, the statements of the accused under section 342 of the CrPC and the other materials on record and then the impugned judgment and order. It is contended by the learned Advocates on behalf of the appellants that the charge is materially defective and the accused-appellants have been prejudiced thereby. Nextly, it is contended by the learned Advocates for the appellants that the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the charges against the appellants vis-a-vis that place, time and the manner of occurrence as alleged by the prosecution by cogent, reliable and sufficient evidence and, as such, impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence cannot be sustained in law and also on facts. Thereafter, it is contended on behalf of the appellants that their conviction has been based on inadmissible evidence, inasmuch as the post-mortem report in this case has not been put into evidence in accordance with law and further there has not been proper and correct recognition of the accused-appellants. The next submission on behalf of the appellants is that the defence case has not been properly considered and there has been misreading and also misapplication of the evidence on record by the learned Sessions Judge and, as a result, there has been complete failure of justice. Lastly, it has been contended by the learned Advocates for the appellants that the learned Sessions Judge ought to have drawn an adverse presumption against the prosecution case for non production of the material witnesses, particularly one Kalpuna, the second wife of the deceased, cog. No. 1102 Unus Ali who brought and identified the deceased before the Doctor, Afsar Uddin, Rehan Uddin, Amjul Haque, Khaled Chowdhury, Imran Khan, Abu Siddique and A Gafur who immediately appeared at the place of occurrence house and saw the occurrence and heard the names of the accused. Consequently, in the facts and circumstances of the case the appellants ought to have been given benefit of doubt.
